newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port sacks 185 strikers, warns others.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port sacks 185 strikers, warns others.

text.p: Colombo port, south Asia's shipping hub, has sacked 185 temporary dock workers who took part in a strike which disrupted work last month, Sri Lanka's Ports and Shipping Ministry said on Thursday.
"Stern action will be taken against those who try to disrupt port operations," a ministry statement said.
The workers who were fired were absent from work on December 27, the day of the strike, without taking leave, it said.
Labour unions organised the strike to oppose plans to lease the port's Queen Elizabeth Quay to Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co (P&O).

The unions have threatened more action unless the government calls off the deal. They say they fear the planned lease would lead to retrenchment and losses by the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA), which runs the port.
The SLPA is holding talks with P&O to turn Queen Elizabeth Quay into a new container terminal to expand capacity and later build a new port adjacent to the present one.

The project, estimated to cost up to $1 billion and take 10 years to build, will see the development of the southern part of the port with at least another six deep-draft berths with a capacity of two million containers per year.
